$comment: Reviewed merge-queue policy for the active development tier.
This file is intentionally separate from branch-protection.json: GitHub's
classic branch-protection API and repository ruleset merge_queue rule are
different API surfaces. Keeping the queue parameters here makes the live
ruleset reviewable without pretending the classic protection payload accepts
Batching posture: one merge-group verification cycle covers up to
max_entries_to_merge compatible candidates; a group forms once that many
candidates wait or min_entries_to_merge_wait_minutes elapses with at least
min_entries_to_merge present. Every queued PR still verifies on its own
entry branch (ALLGREEN); a failing entry is ejected and the entries behind
it are rebuilt, and scripts/check-enqueue-merge-queue.py quarantines a head
that failed in the queue instead of re-queueing it. This supersedes the
one-PR-per-group rollout posture: the original canary precondition is met
(the queue has been live on develop since 2026-08-30; see
values and fails closed on anything else.
